topic: Memory Hierarchy and Caching Strategies: Minimizing Time
explanation: The memory hierarchy structures storage tiers (registers, L1/L2/L3 cache, main memory) to optimize the trade-off between access latency and capacity. Caches are high-speed, low-latency buffers positioned between the CPU and DRAM. Their primary function is to minimize the average memory access time (AMAT). This reduction is achieved by exploiting the principle of locality of reference. Effective caching strategies predict future data requests based on observed temporal locality (reusing recently accessed data) and spatial locality (accessing data near recently accessed addresses) to maximize the cache hit rate.
